security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, reference links, CSS text, or benign words. The executable pipeline template does perform local file writes, and AI review found unvalidated path construction that could let writes or clean operations escape intended directories. No evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, network calls, or malicious command execution was found.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated batch and item identifiers are used in filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers with a strict allowlist, resolve paths, and reject any path that escapes the intended data or output directory.

remediation.issue: The clean stage deletes generated files without a preview or confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the resolved target directory, require explicit confirmation for deletion, and keep cleanup limited to known generated artifact names.

remediation.issue: The template writes local artifacts when users run pipeline stages.
remediation.suggestion: Document every generated file location and add a dry-run mode for stages that create or overwrite artifacts.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Path Components in Pipeline Template
semantic_findings.description: The executable template accepts batch identifiers from the CLI and combines them directly with data and output directories. Parent directory segments in batch or item identifiers could redirect writes or clean-stage deletions outside the intended project folders.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path helpers concatenate CLI-controlled batch_id and item identifiers into filesystem paths, and the clean stage unlinks files below that computed path. The script is user-run and intended for local use, so this is high confidence but not critical.

content.value_statement: Teams often build LLM projects before proving task fit, cost, and pipeline boundaries. This skill guides validation, staged architecture, and iteration plans for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Evaluate whether a task fits LLM strengths before automation begins.
Design staged acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render pipelines.
Use file system state for caching, debugging, and reruns.
Estimate token costs and add practical retry buffers.
Compare single-agent and multi-agent project structures.
Provide a Python template for batch pipeline experimentation.
limitations: The included Python template uses mock LLM responses by default.
Production API calls, authentication, and deployment are left to the user.
The guidance does not guarantee model accuracy or parsing success.
Security hardening is required before using the template with untrusted input.

use_cases.title: Validate a New LLM Idea
use_cases.description: Check task-model fit, acceptable error rates, and expected output shape before writing automation.

use_cases.title: Design a Batch Analysis Pipeline
use_cases.description: Break a large corpus workflow into cacheable stages with clear rerun and debugging points.

use_cases.title: Control Agent Project Costs
use_cases.description: Estimate token usage, choose a simple architecture, and decide when multi-agent complexity is justified.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Task Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this project is suitable for LLM processing. Cover input type, desired output, error tolerance, model knowledge needs, and one manual prototype test.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Pipeline Stages
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a staged LLM pipeline for this workflow. Define acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render stages with artifacts, rerun rules, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Scale and Cost
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing a budget or launch plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate token cost and runtime for this batch project. Include item count assumptions, input and output token estimates, retry buffer, and cost control options.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LLM project architecture. Identify where a single pipeline is enough, where multi-agent work may help, and which complexity should be removed.

output_examples.input: I need to analyze 8,000 support tickets and produce theme summaries.
output: Task-model fit assessment with likely strengths and weak points.
A staged batch pipeline plan with persistent intermediate artifacts.
A cost estimate framework with retry and review buffers.

output_examples.input: Our agent project has many tools and slow runs.
output: A recommendation to test a simpler baseline before adding tools.
Criteria for keeping, merging, or removing specialized tools.
An iteration plan that compares quality, latency, and cost.

output_examples.input: I want a reusable template for batch LLM processing.
output: Stage definitions for data acquisition, prompt preparation, model calls, parsing, and rendering.
File-based state management guidance for caching and debugging.
Notes on parser tolerance and manual validation before scaling.

best_practices: Run a manual prototype with one representative item before writing automation.
Keep each pipeline stage idempotent, observable, and independently runnable.
Track token costs and parsing failures during development, not after launch.
anti_patterns: Do not build a full pipeline before proving the model can handle the task.
Do not combine acquisition, model calls, parsing, and rendering into one opaque step.
Do not use multi-agent architecture only to imitate human team roles.

faq.question: Does this skill call external LLM APIs directly?
faq.answer: No. The included template returns mock responses until the user adds an API integration.

faq.question: Can this help with Claude and Claude Code projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Claude, Claude Code, Codex, and other agent-capable tools.

faq.question: Is the pipeline template production ready?
faq.answer: No. It is a starting template and needs validation, security controls, and real API handling.

faq.question: When should I use a multi-agent design?
faq.answer: Use it when context isolation or parallel exploration improves quality enough to justify cost.

faq.question: How does the skill support cost planning?
faq.answer: It explains token estimation, output length assumptions, retry buffers, and simpler architecture choices.

faq.question: What should I do before scaling a batch job?
faq.answer: Validate one item manually, inspect output quality, test parsing, and estimate total token cost.
